clue.text: Give up on account of work

parts.note: for can mean because of or on account of
to go is to work or function, as a machine does

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a plan because of their job.
explanation.definitionFit: To forgo something is to do without it, to relinquish it voluntarily.

clue.text: Set a standard weight

parts.note: a standard is a flag or banner
a stone is a British unit of weight, fourteen pounds

explanation.surface: Someone fixes a normal heaviness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' is a noun: a set (or sett) is a paving block.
explanation.definitionFit: A sett is a squared paving block, just as a flagstone is a flat slab for paving.

clue.text: Arm in plaster if leg is broken?

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words plaster if leg

explanation.surface: A limb in a cast, if a leg has fractured?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arm' and 'leg' paint a hospital scene; arm here is a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A rifle is a firearm, a weapon.

clue.text: 9 points separate couple in scramble

indicators.note: separate says the points split the scrambled word apart
scramble means the letters of couple are jumbled

parts.note: E and N are compass points, east and north

explanation.surface: Nine points divide two people in a struggle.
explanation.walkthrough: COUPLE scrambled gives OPULCE, split by EN; '9' refers to the answer at 9, AFFLUENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulence and affluence both mean great wealth and luxury.

clue.text: Sort of dive some transport drivers hope to avoid

definitions.text: some transport drivers hope to avoid

explanation.surface: A diving style that lorry drivers would rather not perform.
explanation.definitionFit: A jackknife is a dive bending double in mid-air, and also the accident where an articulated lorry's trailer swings round against its cab.

clue.text: Worthless craft

explanation.surface: A useless boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Junk is rubbish of no value, and a junk is a flat-bottomed Chinese sailing ship.

clue.text: A sweet little child. J.R.? Gosh!

parts.note: ch is a short form of child
J.R. Ewing is the villain of the TV soap Dallas
by gum is an old exclamation like gosh

explanation.surface: Admiring an adorable toddler, someone exclaims about a famous name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A sweet little child' reads as one phrase, but 'A sweet' is the definition. J.R. Ewing is the oil baron of the American soap Dallas; 'by gum' is a northern English oath.
explanation.definitionFit: Chewing gum is a confection one chews but does not swallow.

clue.text: Light the French sort first

indicators.note: first says the word for sort comes before the French word

parts.note: kind means sort or type
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A Frenchman lights the fire first.
explanation.definitionFit: To kindle is to set alight, to make a fire burn.

clue.text: Foolish about mother, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: about says the foolish word goes around the word for mother

parts.note: idiotic means foolish
ma is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: Someone is silly about their mum, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a manner of speaking' looks like a throwaway phrase meaning 'so to speak', but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiomatic means using natural expressions peculiar to a language, so characteristic of a way of speaking.

clue.text: Happening to require key on opening

indicators.note: on, in a down clue, puts the key above the opening

parts.note: E is a musical key
a vent is an opening or outlet

explanation.surface: It seems a key is needed to open something.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is something that happens, an occurrence.

clue.text: Cause of ill-feeling in a criminal's wealth

indicators.note: in puts the cause of ill-feeling within the words a criminal's

parts.note: a fence is a criminal who deals in stolen goods
influenza, flu for short, makes one feel ill

explanation.surface: A crook's riches are the source of resentment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ill-feeling' suggests resentment, but here it is literal: physical illness, caused by flu.
explanation.definitionFit: Affluence is abundance of money and possessions, prosperity.

clue.text: One is unusually sound

indicators.note: unusually says the letters of one is appear in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A single thing is strangely healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Noise is any sound, especially a loud or unwanted one.

clue.text: A more oblique means of fixing the joint?

explanation.surface: Something slanting further is a way of securing a piece of meat for roasting.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense splits the word as skew plus the comparative ending -er.
explanation.definitionFit: Skew means slanting, so the comparative is more slanting; a skewer is also a pin pushed through meat to hold it together.

clue.text: One in 400 in Rome

parts.note: 400 in Roman numerals is CD, the letters for Corps ..., so one in it is a member of the ... corps

explanation.surface: A single person among four hundred living in the Italian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rome' suggests the city, but it only tells you to read 400 as a Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Corps Diplomatique are envoys representing their country abroad.

clue.text: For good measure, go in for body-building

explanation.surface: Add a bit extra by taking up weight training.
explanation.walkthrough: The held clue had a stray 'James'' that the printed page does not show.
explanation.definitionFit: A makeweight is something added to bring a quantity up to the required amount; to make weight is to build up the body to a set mass.

clue.text: Ask too much about the attack

parts.note: over can mean about or concerning, as in a row over money
a charge is an attack, as by cavalry

explanation.surface: Someone makes excessive demands concerning an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: To overcharge is to demand a price higher than is fair.

clue.text: "Time's up!" In exam I produced only part of paper

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, means the word for time is read from bottom to top

parts.note: tide is an old word for time, as in Christmastide

indicators.note: In says the letter I goes inside the word for an exam

parts.note: an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: An invigilator calls time and a candidate has finished only part of the paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses TIDE to EDIT; I inside ORAL gives ORIAL. 'Paper' here is a newspaper, not an exam paper.
explanation.definitionFit: An editorial is a newspaper article giving the editor's opinion.

clue.text: Boss seen in a boiled shirt

explanation.surface: An employer is spotted wearing a starched formal shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: A boiled shirt is a stiff-fronted dress shirt, fastened with ornamental studs.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss is a raised knob or ornamental stud, and a stud is also the button fastening a dress shirt front.

clue.text: Run down variable gradient to end of line

indicators.note: variable means the letters of gradient can vary in order
end of picks the last letter of line

explanation.surface: Cycle downhill on a changing slope to the end of the route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variable' rearranges GRADIENT to DENIGRAT, and 'end of' adds the E of line.
explanation.definitionFit: To run down someone is to disparage or belittle them.

clue.text: Insect burrowing in level stretch can spoil a lawn

indicators.note: burrowing in means the insect digs its way inside the level stretch

parts.note: a plain is a flat expanse of land
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A tunnelling insect on flat ground can ruin the grass.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is descriptive: a thing that can spoil a lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Plantain is a broad-leaved weed that spreads across turf.

clue.text: Charged retrospectively — that's bad

indicators.note: retrospectively means looking back, so the word for charged is read backwards

parts.note: an electrically charged wire is live

explanation.surface: Someone accused after the event calls it wicked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charged' suggests an accusation; it is the electrical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Evil means wicked, morally wrong.

clue.text: Are without a host in US party

indicators.note: without says the letter named next is removed from are

parts.note: taken as written, the letter removed
a publican is the landlord or host of a pub

explanation.surface: Are you without a host at an American political gathering?
explanation.walkthrough: A publican is the keeper of a British pub.
explanation.definitionFit: The Republicans are one of the two main political parties in the United States, and the word names that party.

clue.text: Spice provided by one mad Margaret

parts.note: a nut is a mad person
Meg is a short form of Margaret

explanation.surface: Seasoning supplied by a crazy woman called Margaret.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutmeg is the aromatic seed of a tropical tree, grated as a seasoning.

clue.text: Movie mogul taking half of it could be corrupted

indicators.note: could be signals that the letters of corrupted are rearranged, with the extra piece taken away
half of means one of the two letters of it, here its second

explanation.surface: A film tycoon receiving his share might be bribed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' means the T (half of 'it') is removed from CORRUPTED, and 'could be' rearranges the remaining letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A producer is the person who finances and oversees the making of a film.

clue.text: Half of Welsh Nationalists formed by the cloth

explanation.surface: Half the Welsh nationalist movement was made by the clergy.
explanation.walkthrough: Plaid Cymru is the Welsh nationalist party; 'the cloth' suggests the clergy, but it is fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: The first word of the Welsh party's name; also a tartan woollen fabric.

clue.text: In conclusion, 21 does

parts.note: the solution to 21 (the spice) finishes on the letter G

explanation.surface: Finally, clue 21 acts.
explanation.walkthrough: Clue 21's answer is the spice NUTMEG, which ends in G.
explanation.definitionFit: An ending is a conclusion or finish.

clue.text: "We have done but greenly In hugger-mugger to —— him" (Hamlet)

definitions.text: "We have done but greenly In hugger-mugger to —— him" (Hamlet)

parts.words: "We have done but greenly In hugger-mugger to —— him" (Hamlet)
parts.note: Claudius on Polonius's hasty secret burial: the missing word before him is the verb meaning to bury

clue.text: Brought up to the sound of common money

indicators.note: to the sound of says the word is heard rather than seen

parts.note: bread is slang, common speech, for money

explanation.surface: Raised hearing the jingle of everyday cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Bred means raised or reared, as a child or animal.

clue.text: It's obvious there's a split across the island

indicators.note: across places the first piece beside the island, reading left to right

parts.note: to ax (axe) is to chop or split wood
IOM is the abbreviation for the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: Clearly the island is divided down the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man is a British island in the Irish Sea, abbreviated IOM.
explanation.definitionFit: An axiom is a self-evident truth needing no proof.

clue.text: Giant could give Agag a turn

indicators.note: could give signals that the letters of Agag a turn can be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: A huge figure might make the biblical King Agag a turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' looks like the anagram signal, but it is part of the fodder; Agag was a king in the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Gargantua is the enormous giant of Rabelais's satire.

clue.text: Glad of something to brighten us up indeed

indicators.note: the in of indeed is read as a separate word saying the rest goes inside deed

parts.note: taken as written, the last four letters of indeed
a light brightens a room for us

explanation.surface: Happy about something that cheers us, truly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'indeed' must be split as 'in deed': LIGHT goes inside DEED.
explanation.definitionFit: Delighted means greatly pleased, very happy.

clue.text: Tender shark

explanation.surface: A gentle predator of the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: To tend the sick is to care for them; the nurse shark is a slow bottom-dwelling species.
